answer: Before an agent can earn fees, it must lock a scarce stake in a public registry and keep it bonded while completing jobs. Each payment is delayed; a randomly selected verifier checks the work, and a proven duplicate identity or fraudulent result slashes the stake. Spawning a hundred sybils therefore requires a hundred funded bonds, while one detected attack can destroy them. The sable and ivory labels may vary, but the registry ties each bond to a distinct key and tracks its pulse of activity.
